turns.text: I am treating a 50-year-old female with a 4 cm vulvar cancer (squamous cell, Stage II, depth of invasion 5 mm, 2 mm margins after radical vulvectomy). She has a positive left inguinal sentinel lymph node (0.3 mm deposit). She has a history of morbid obesity (BMI 48, lost 30 kg with bariatric surgery 2 years ago, current BMI 35). She has residual redundant skin in the inguinal region. She has well-controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.0%). She needs adjuvant therapy. Should I recommend adjuvant radiation to the vulvar bed and inguinal regions? What brachytherapy approach could address the vulvar bed? How does her body habitus affect radiation planning?

58yo F, recurrent high-grade serous ovarian cancer (platinum-sensitive, 20mo relapse). 3.5cm vaginal + 1.5cm peritoneal deposit. Post-6x carbo/gem with response. Debulking + IP chemo + VBT boost. Prior bowel obstruction.
